purpose: Provide a machine-readable knowledge base for locating, ranking, and evaluating documents and knowledge across lexical, neural, and hybrid retrieval, with evaluation, governance, and session-bounded workflow control.
assumptions: No observed dataset, expert judgment, or benchmark evidence was supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors.
Scope is the knowledge-discovery lens of IR: how to locate, rank, and evaluate documents and knowledge.
Standard IR references (Manning et al. 2008; Baeza-Yates & Ribeiro-Neto 2011; Croft et al. 2009) inform framing only, not as cited measurements.
Each node is bounded to one heavy reasoning session with a handoff artifact.
exclusions: Full-text crawling and web-scale infrastructure engineering details.
Generative model pretraining methodology beyond retrieval grounding.
Domain-specific legal/compliance review beyond access-rights scoping.
Recommendation systems and personalization beyond ranking feedback.

competency_questions.question: How is a raw user information need turned into a formalized, measurable retrieval target?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: check INFO_NEED/QUERY_PROC outputs map to success criteria

competency_questions.question: What defines the document collection boundary, freshness, and access rights to be searched?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: check CORPUS_SCOPE produces a scoped corpus definition

competency_questions.question: How are documents tokenized, normalized, and indexed for efficient lookup?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: check DOC_REP and INV_INDEX dependency chain

competency_questions.question: Which index structure (inverted vs ANN) fits a given query and latency profile?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: check INV_INDEX/ANN_INDEX and their conflict axis

competency_questions.question: When should dense or hybrid retrieval be used over lexical retrieval?
How are first-stage retrieval, reranking, and query processing composed into a ranking pipeline?
How does retrieval quality bound retrieval-augmented generation faithfulness?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: check RERANK->RAG dependency and RAG acceptance tests

competency_questions.question: How are relevance judgments created and used to compute ranking metrics?
How are reusable test collections built and kept unbiased via pooling?
Which metric and significance test fit a given task, and how is validity governed?
How are corpus scope and serving constraints reconciled with retrieval depth?
How is interaction feedback used to adapt ranking without amplifying bias?
How is ranking fairness and exposure bias assessed against effectiveness?

glossary.definition: Probabilistic lexical ranking function over term frequency and inverse document frequency with length normalization.
First-stage retrieval using learned query/document embeddings compared in a vector space.
Second-stage rescoring of a candidate set, typically with a cross-encoder.
Normalized discounted cumulative gain; rank-sensitive metric over graded relevance.
TREC method of judging the union of top-k documents from multiple systems to build a reusable collection.
Human-assigned label of how relevant a document is to a query.
Retrieval-augmented generation; generation conditioned on retrieved evidence.
Combination of lexical and dense ranked lists via score or rank fusion.
Map from terms to postings lists of documents containing them.
Approximate nearest neighbor index over embeddings for sublinear vector search.

evidence_label_policy.rationale: No OBSERVED_DATA or benchmark evidence supplied, so only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Model heuristic priors over information-retrieval practice grounded in standard IR textbooks and TREC methodology.
grounding_limits: scores are heuristic priors not measurements

nodes.definition: Capture and operationalize the searcher's underlying information need into queries and success criteria.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: user task type reclassified (navigational vs informational vs transactional)

pros.claim: specifies what 'found' means before ranking is tuned
pros.example: define success as nDCG@10>=0.6 for known test queries

cons.claim: intent inference is uncertain without interaction logs

failure_modes: misclassified intent yields wrong retrieval model choice
success criteria omitted, evaluation undefined
acceptance_tests: confirm need maps to >=1 measurable success criterion
verify intent taxonomy covers the query sample

nodes.definition: Define the document collection, its boundaries, freshness, and access constraints to be searched.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new high-value source becomes available or a source is deprecated

pros.claim: bounds evaluation universe, preventing leakage between train/test corpora
pros.example: exclude post-cutoff docs from a TREC-style judged pool

cons.claim: over-broad corpus inflates index cost and dilutes precision
cons.example: crawling whole web when only docs from one journal are relevant

failure_modes: scope omits authoritative source class
license-restricted docs indexed without rights
acceptance_tests: confirm corpus boundary is explicit and license-checked
verify freshness policy is stated
revisit_triggers: source set or license terms change

nodes.definition: Choose tokenization, normalization, and field structure that turn raw documents into indexable units.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: language mix or domain vocabulary shifts materially

pros.claim: consistent analysis chain lets query and doc terms match
pros.example: apply same Porter stemmer to query and index

failure_modes: analyzer mismatch between query and index time
unicode normalization drops diacritics meaningfully
acceptance_tests: verify query-time and index-time analyzers are identical
revisit_triggers: vocabulary drift detected in term stats

nodes.definition: Build inverted-list/posting structures and term dictionaries enabling sublinear lexical lookup.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: corpus size growth changes compression/sharding tradeoffs

pros.claim: postings + skip pointers give sublinear conjunctive query evaluation
pros.example: skip lists cut intersection cost on long postings

cons.claim: index rebuild cost is high under frequent updates
cons.example: full reindex needed when analyzer changes

failure_modes: postings corruption from interrupted merge
term-statistics stale after incremental updates
acceptance_tests: verify document frequency counts match recomputed corpus stats
revisit_triggers: corpus grows past a sharding threshold

nodes.definition: Construct approximate-nearest-neighbor indexes (HNSW/IVF/PQ) over dense embeddings for semantic recall.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: embedding model changes, invalidating the vector space

pros.claim: ANN gives semantic recall lexical index cannot reach
pros.example: HNSW retrieves paraphrases lacking shared terms

cons.claim: approximation drops true neighbors at low ef_search
cons.example: recall collapses when IVF nprobe set too low

failure_modes: index built against a now-replaced embedding model
recall/latency target not met at scale
acceptance_tests: recall@k measured on held-out judged pairs vs target
confirm index versioned with its embedding model id

nodes.definition: Score documents with term-weighting models (TF-IDF, BM25, vector space) over the inverted index.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: term-statistics distribution shifts or BM25 k1/b need retuning

pros.claim: BM25 is a strong, cheap, explainable first-stage baseline
pros.example: BM25 routinely competitive on TREC ad-hoc tasks

cons.claim: lexical mismatch misses semantically relevant docs
cons.example: query 'heart attack' misses doc saying 'myocardial infarction'

failure_modes: BM25 parameters left at defaults for an atypical corpus
idf skew from a polluted document-frequency table
acceptance_tests: confirm BM25 baseline reproduces published metric on a known collection

nodes.definition: Encode queries and documents into a shared embedding space for semantic first-stage retrieval.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: domain shift degrades embedding relevance or new training pairs arrive

pros.claim: captures semantic matches beyond exact terms
pros.example: DPR retrieves answer passages without lexical overlap

cons.claim: out-of-domain queries collapse to generic neighbors
cons.example: medical query embeds poorly with a general-web encoder

failure_modes: train/serve embedding model mismatch
domain shift unmonitored, silent recall loss
acceptance_tests: measure nDCG vs BM25 baseline on judged queries
confirm encoder identical at train and serve time

nodes.definition: Re-score a candidate set with a high-cost cross-encoder to refine top-k ordering.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: candidate-set recall ceiling or latency budget changes

pros.claim: cross-attention captures fine query-doc interaction first-stage misses
pros.example: reranker fixes ordering of near-duplicate top results

cons.claim: cannot recover documents missing from the candidate set
cons.example: relevant doc dropped by first stage is unrecoverable

failure_modes: reranker latency exceeds budget at top-k
candidate recall too low to benefit from reranking
acceptance_tests: confirm reranked nDCG@10 improves over first-stage within latency SLO

nodes.definition: Couple retrieval with a generative model so answers are grounded in retrieved evidence.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: retrieval quality or generator version changes the grounding faithfulness

pros.claim: grounds generation in retrieved evidence, reducing hallucination
pros.example: answer cites the retrieved passage that supports each claim

cons.claim: bad retrieval propagates wrong evidence into fluent answers
cons.example: irrelevant passage yields confident but unsupported answer

failure_modes: retrieved context exceeds window and truncates evidence
ungrounded claims pass without citation check
acceptance_tests: verify each answer claim is attributable to a retrieved passage
confirm faithfulness metric meets threshold

nodes.definition: Produce graded or binary relevance labels for query-document pairs to ground evaluation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: annotation guideline revised or inter-annotator agreement drops

pros.claim: graded judgments enable nDCG and rank-sensitive evaluation

cons.claim: subjective labels carry annotator bias and disagreement
cons.example: two assessors disagree on borderline topical match

failure_modes: guideline ambiguity yields low kappa
label set not representative of query distribution
acceptance_tests: confirm inter-annotator agreement above threshold
verify judged pool covers evaluated systems
revisit_triggers: new system pooled that may surface unjudged docs

nodes.definition: Assemble reusable test collections via pooling judged documents across systems (TREC methodology).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new system retrieves many unjudged documents, exposing pool bias

pros.claim: pooling yields reusable collections evaluable for new systems
pros.example: TREC pools let later systems be scored without re-judging

cons.claim: shallow pools bias against systems not in the pool
cons.example: novel system penalized for surfacing unjudged relevant docs

failure_modes: pool depth too shallow for fair reuse
collection reused beyond its valid system population
acceptance_tests: confirm pool depth and contributing runs are documented
verify residual-collection bias is estimated
revisit_triggers: new system class evaluated against old pool
judged fraction at depth k drops

nodes.definition: Define and compute rank-sensitive effectiveness metrics: nDCG, MAP, MRR, precision/recall.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: task changes which metric is primary (e.g. known-item -> MRR)

pros.claim: nDCG with graded labels rewards correct rank ordering
pros.example: nDCG@10 distinguishes systems that bury relevant docs

cons.claim: wrong metric for the task misranks systems
cons.example: MAP misleads for known-item tasks where MRR fits

failure_modes: metric chosen mismatches the user task
gain/discount settings undocumented, scores incomparable
acceptance_tests: confirm primary metric matches the information-need type
verify metric implementation matches a reference

nodes.definition: Apply significance tests and confidence intervals so metric deltas reflect real differences.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: query sample size changes the achievable statistical power

pros.claim: paired tests separate real gains from query-sample noise
pros.example: bootstrap CI shows a 0.01 nDCG delta is not significant

cons.claim: many comparisons without correction inflate false positives

failure_modes: uncorrected multiple comparisons
too few queries for adequate power
acceptance_tests: confirm test is paired and multiple-comparison corrected
verify query count gives target power

nodes.definition: Transform raw queries via parsing, expansion, spell-correction, and reformulation before retrieval.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: query log reveals new misspelling or intent patterns

pros.claim: expansion bridges vocabulary gap between query and docs

cons.claim: over-expansion injects noise and drifts intent
cons.example: adding loosely related synonyms degrades precision

failure_modes: expansion drifts query intent
spell-correction over-corrects valid rare terms
acceptance_tests: confirm expansion improves recall without precision collapse on judged set

nodes.definition: Combine lexical and dense signals via score fusion (e.g. reciprocal rank fusion) for robust recall.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: relative strength of lexical vs dense signal shifts on new queries

pros.claim: fusion recovers docs either signal alone would miss
pros.example: RRF combines BM25 and DPR for higher recall@100

cons.claim: naive score addition is dominated by uncalibrated scales
cons.example: raw BM25+cosine sum skewed by scale mismatch

failure_modes: score scales not normalized before fusion
fusion weights overfit to a small dev set
acceptance_tests: confirm fused recall and nDCG beat both single-signal baselines
revisit_triggers: new retrieval signal added to the ensemble

nodes.definition: Serve ranking under latency, throughput, and freshness SLOs in production.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: traffic pattern or SLO target changes the retrieval depth budget

pros.claim: tiered retrieval meets latency by deepening only when needed
pros.example: cheap BM25 prefilter caps cross-encoder calls

cons.claim: latency cuts force shallow candidate sets, hurting recall
cons.example: tight SLO truncates reranking to top-20

failure_modes: tail latency violates SLO under load
stale cache serves outdated rankings
acceptance_tests: confirm p99 latency within SLO at target QPS

nodes.definition: Use explicit/implicit feedback (clicks, judgments) to adapt ranking over time.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: click distribution shifts due to presentation or population change

pros.claim: implicit feedback scales relevance signal cheaply
pros.example: click models infer relevance from skip/click patterns

cons.claim: position and presentation bias contaminate click signal
cons.example: top result over-clicked regardless of true relevance

failure_modes: click bias uncorrected in training signal
feedback loop amplifies popular-but-irrelevant docs
acceptance_tests: confirm click signal is bias-corrected before use in ranking

nodes.definition: Assess and mitigate ranking bias and inequitable exposure across documents and groups.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: regulatory or stakeholder fairness criteria are introduced or revised

pros.claim: exposure audits surface systemic ranking inequities
pros.example: measures whether minority-source docs get fair exposure

cons.claim: fairness-effectiveness tradeoff lacks a single optimum
cons.example: boosting exposure can lower top-line nDCG

failure_modes: fairness criteria undefined for the domain
diversity intervention silently harms relevance
acceptance_tests: confirm exposure metric defined and audited against a policy
verify fairness-effectiveness tradeoff is documented

nodes.definition: Govern evaluation integrity: train/test leakage, reproducibility, and benchmark overfitting controls.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: evidence of test-set contamination or repeated tuning on the test collection

pros.claim: leakage and overfit guards keep reported gains trustworthy
pros.example: held-out collection prevents tuning on the test set

cons.example: freezing the test set blocks fast hill-climbing

failure_modes: test collection reused until overfit
train/test split leaks via shared documents
acceptance_tests: confirm no document overlap between tuning and test pools
verify results reproduce from logged configs
revisit_triggers: repeated evaluations on the same test set detected

edges.why_related: retrieval model must target a formalized information need
edges.resolution_rule: information_need spec governs; finalize need before tuning

edges.why_related: representation choices depend on the scoped corpus
edges.benefit_of_coupling: analyzer matched to corpus language mix
edges.example: scope fixes language set before tokenizer choice
edges.resolution_rule: scope dominates; lock corpus before representation

edges.why_related: index is built over the chosen token representation
edges.resolution_rule: representation locked before index build

edges.why_related: lexical scoring requires the inverted index and term stats
edges.benefit_of_coupling: BM25 reads df/tf from the index
edges.example: BM25 needs document frequencies from postings
edges.resolution_rule: index term-statistics must be current before scoring

edges.why_related: ANN index is built from the dense encoder embeddings
edges.resolution_rule: encoder version pins the ANN index

edges.why_related: dense model must encode toward the defined need
edges.resolution_rule: need spec governs training-pair selection

edges.why_related: reranking consumes the lexical candidate set
edges.resolution_rule: first-stage recall gates reranking value

edges.why_related: reranking can consume dense candidates too
edges.resolution_rule: candidate recall ceiling bounds reranking

edges.why_related: generation is grounded on reranked top-k
edges.example: reranked passages fill the RAG context
edges.resolution_rule: retrieval quality gates generation grounding

edges.why_related: labels are judged against the defined need
edges.example: assessors judge relevance to the stated topic
edges.resolution_rule: need spec defines relevance criteria

edges.why_related: test collection assembled from judgments
edges.example: TREC pool built from assessor judgments
edges.resolution_rule: judgments must exist before pooling

edges.why_related: rank metrics are computed against judgments
edges.resolution_rule: labels precede metric computation

edges.why_related: significance testing operates on metric scores
edges.resolution_rule: metrics computed before significance tests

edges.why_related: query processing serves the formalized need
edges.resolution_rule: need spec bounds query reformulation

edges.why_related: query analysis must match document analysis
edges.example: same stemmer for query and docs
edges.resolution_rule: representation governs query-time analysis

edges.why_related: fusion needs the lexical candidate ranking
edges.resolution_rule: lexical ranking required before fusion

edges.why_related: fusion needs the dense candidate ranking
edges.resolution_rule: dense ranking required before fusion

edges.why_related: serving exposes the fused ranking pipeline
edges.resolution_rule: ranking pipeline finalized before serving

edges.why_related: feedback is collected from served interactions
edges.resolution_rule: serving must run before feedback collection

edges.why_related: fairness audit extends the metric framework
edges.benefit_of_coupling: exposure metrics build on ranking metrics
edges.resolution_rule: metric framework precedes fairness audit

edges.why_related: validity governance audits the test collection
edges.example: leakage check on the reused pool
edges.resolution_rule: governance reviews collection before reuse

edges.why_related: governance relies on significance verdicts
edges.resolution_rule: significance precedes validity sign-off

edges.why_related: query processing changes lexical retrieval recall/precision
edges.example: PRF adds terms, shifting BM25 results
edges.resolution_rule: prefer recall gain only if precision holds on judged set

edges.why_related: fusion depth changes serving latency
edges.resolution_rule: cap fusion depth to fit latency SLO

edges.why_related: reranking depth changes serving latency
edges.resolution_rule: tier reranking depth to the latency budget

edges.why_related: feedback signal changes dense model training quality
edges.resolution_rule: bias-correct feedback before training

edges.why_related: latency SLO bounds how much reranking is allowed
edges.resolution_rule: SLO bounds reranking depth; widen only with approval

edges.why_related: corpus scope bounds which docs can be judged
edges.example: only in-corpus docs enter the pool
edges.resolution_rule: scope limits the judgment universe

edges.why_related: judgment depth constrains pool reusability
edges.resolution_rule: judgment depth bounds collection reuse claims

edges.why_related: lexical and dense compete as first-stage models for budget and recall
edges.benefit_of_coupling: each covers the other's blind spots
edges.example: budget split between BM25 and DPR
edges.resolution_rule: resolve via hybrid fusion rather than picking one when both add recall

edges.why_related: reranking quality conflicts with latency budget
edges.resolution_rule: latency SLO dominates; cap reranking depth, escalate to widen SLO

edges.why_related: embedding recall conflicts with ANN approximation/latency
edges.example: recall vs latency on HNSW ef
edges.resolution_rule: tune ef to meet recall floor at latency budget

edges.why_related: effectiveness maximization conflicts with exposure fairness
edges.resolution_rule: apply fairness floor as a constraint on effectiveness optimization

edges.why_related: RAG iteration speed conflicts with evaluation validity controls
edges.example: freezing eval set vs fast prompt tuning
edges.resolution_rule: governance dominates for release; allow sandboxed iteration off the frozen set

edges.why_related: broad corpus scope conflicts with dense in-domain quality
edges.example: general encoder on a niche corpus
edges.resolution_rule: narrow scope or domain-adapt the encoder when precision drops

edges.why_related: frame the need before scoping the corpus to search
edges.risk_of_conflict: scoping first may exclude needed sources
edges.example: define task before choosing the collection
edges.resolution_rule: sequence need->scope to avoid corpus rework

edges.why_related: evaluation results can trigger revisiting query processing
edges.resolution_rule: stop revisiting after 2 cycles with no significant gain

edges.why_related: governance findings can trigger metric redefinition
edges.resolution_rule: stop after metric is revalidated on a clean collection

edges.why_related: labeling and metrics are tightly coupled evaluation concerns
edges.benefit_of_coupling: plan them together to avoid mismatch
edges.risk_of_conflict: treating them as one node hides annotation cost
edges.example: graded labels paired with nDCG settings
edges.resolution_rule: keep distinct nodes; coordinate gain/discount with label scale

conflict_axes.trigger: limited compute/latency budget forces choosing or weighting first-stage retrievers
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: prefer hybrid fusion when both add judged recall; if budget forbids, keep lexical baseline and add dense only where it lifts nDCG significantly
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: dense adds no significant nDCG gain yet doubles serving cost
conflict_axes.example: BM25 vs DPR under a fixed GPU budget for first-stage recall

conflict_axes.trigger: cross-encoder reranking depth pushes tail latency past the SLO
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: latency SLO dominates; cap reranking depth, use cascade tiers, escalate to widen SLO only with approval
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: p99 latency exceeds SLO after depth reduction
conflict_axes.example: reranking top-100 vs a 50ms p99 budget

conflict_axes.trigger: raising ef_search/nprobe for recall raises latency and memory
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: tune ANN parameters to the minimum recall floor that meets the latency budget; re-quantize before sacrificing recall
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: recall floor unreachable within latency/memory budget
conflict_axes.example: HNSW ef_search tradeoff between recall@100 and latency

conflict_axes.dominance_logic: treat fairness as a constraint floor; maximize effectiveness subject to meeting the exposure floor
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: no ranking meets both the fairness floor and the effectiveness target
conflict_axes.example: diversity reranking trims nDCG to raise minority-source exposure

conflict_axes.trigger: fast prompt/retrieval tuning risks overfitting the frozen evaluation set
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: governance dominates for release decisions; permit rapid iteration only on a sandbox split off the frozen collection
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: release requested without a clean held-out validity check
conflict_axes.example: tuning RAG prompts against the test set inflates faithfulness scores

conflict_axes.trigger: broadening corpus scope dilutes a general encoder's in-domain precision
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: narrow scope or domain-adapt the encoder when in-domain nDCG drops below target
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: in-domain precision falls below target after scope broadening
conflict_axes.example: a general-web encoder underperforms on a niche medical corpus

conflict_axes.trigger: query expansion raises recall but injects noise that lowers precision
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: accept expansion only if judged precision is not significantly harmed while recall improves
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: expansion lowers judged precision below the acceptable floor
conflict_axes.example: PRF adds terms that drift a 'jaguar' query toward the wrong sense

conflict_axes.trigger: using cheap implicit feedback at scale imports position/presentation bias into evaluation and training
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: require bias correction before click signal enters metrics or training; otherwise prefer judged labels
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: click-based metric diverges materially from judged metric
conflict_axes.example: top-position clicks inflate apparent relevance regardless of true quality

edge_cases.trigger: query-time analyzer differs from index-time analyzer
edge_cases.failure_mode: silent recall loss from non-matching terms
edge_cases.example: index stems but query does not, so 'running' misses 'run'
edge_cases.detection_method: diff query and index analyzer configs and assert equality on a probe set

edge_cases.trigger: incremental updates leave document-frequency statistics stale
edge_cases.example: new docs added but df not recomputed, skewing rare-term weights
edge_cases.detection_method: recompute corpus df sample and compare to index stats within tolerance

edge_cases.trigger: embedding model replaced without rebuilding the ANN index
edge_cases.failure_mode: vectors and index come from different spaces
edge_cases.example: encoder v2 queries searched against a v1-built HNSW index
edge_cases.detection_method: assert ANN index embedding_model_id equals the serving encoder id

edge_cases.trigger: retrieved evidence exceeds the generator context window
edge_cases.example: top-20 long passages overflow the window, dropping the cited one
edge_cases.detection_method: assert assembled context token count <= window and required passages retained

edge_cases.trigger: a new system surfaces many unjudged documents
edge_cases.failure_mode: reused pool unfairly scores the new system low
edge_cases.example: a novel dense system retrieves relevant docs absent from a lexical-era pool
edge_cases.detection_method: measure judged fraction at depth k for the new run and flag below threshold

edge_cases.trigger: primary metric does not match the information-need type
edge_cases.failure_mode: systems misranked for the actual task
edge_cases.example: MAP used for a known-item task where MRR is appropriate
edge_cases.detection_method: check primary metric against the declared need type in INFO_NEED output

edge_cases.trigger: tuning repeatedly on the test collection
edge_cases.failure_mode: benchmark overfit, reported gains do not generalize
edge_cases.example: dozens of ablations selected on the same test qrels
edge_cases.detection_method: track number of evaluations on the frozen set and assert a held-out split exists
resolution: freeze test set and use a dev split

edge_cases.trigger: many system comparisons without multiple-comparison correction
edge_cases.detection_method: assert correction applied when comparison count exceeds two

edge_cases.trigger: latency cuts force candidate sets too shallow
edge_cases.failure_mode: recall collapses, reranking has nothing to fix
edge_cases.example: SLO truncates first-stage to top-10, missing relevant docs
edge_cases.detection_method: monitor recall@k at served depth against the offline recall floor
resolution: raise candidate depth via cheaper first stage

edge_cases.trigger: uncorrected click feedback fed back into ranking
edge_cases.failure_mode: popularity feedback loop amplifies non-relevant popular docs
edge_cases.example: top result over-clicked due to position, then boosted further
edge_cases.detection_method: compare click-derived ranking shifts against judged relevance on a control set

edge_cases.trigger: out-of-scope or post-cutoff documents enter the judged pool
edge_cases.failure_mode: evaluation universe inconsistent with served corpus
edge_cases.example: a post-cutoff doc judged and counted against a frozen corpus
edge_cases.detection_method: assert every judged doc id is within the scoped corpus and freshness window

workflow.objective: formalize the information need and scope the corpus
gates: need maps to measurable success criteria
acceptance_tests: confirm need->criteria mapping exists
workflow.do_first_because: high irreversibility framing must stabilize before any model or index work

workflow.objective: define document representation and build the lexical index
acceptance_tests: confirm analyzer parity on a probe set
workflow.do_first_because: representation must precede indexing to avoid full reindex rework

workflow.objective: train/select the dense encoder and build the ANN index
gates: ann index pinned to encoder version
acceptance_tests: confirm index embedding_model_id matches encoder
workflow.do_first_because: dense path can proceed in parallel with lexical indexing once need is fixed

workflow.objective: establish first-stage lexical, dense, and fused ranking with query processing
acceptance_tests: confirm fused recall@100 exceeds both baselines
workflow.do_first_because: first-stage recall ceiling gates all downstream reranking and generation quality

gates: each answer claim attributable to a retrieved passage
acceptance_tests: confirm faithfulness above threshold
workflow.do_first_because: generation must be built on a validated retrieval stage to stay grounded

workflow.objective: create relevance judgments and build a reusable test collection
acceptance_tests: confirm agreement and pool depth documented
workflow.do_first_because: labels and pools are evaluation foundations and can proceed alongside ranking work

workflow.objective: compute task-appropriate metrics and significance tests
acceptance_tests: confirm metric-task match and paired corrected test
workflow.do_first_because: metrics must be defined and tested before any locking of model choices

workflow.objective: audit evaluation validity and ranking fairness
acceptance_tests: confirm held-out split and exposure audit completed
workflow.do_first_because: validity and fairness governance must pass before serving and lock decisions

workflow.objective: deploy the ranking pipeline under latency and freshness SLOs
gates: p99 latency within SLO at target QPS
acceptance_tests: confirm p99 SLO met under load
workflow.do_first_because: serving is downstream of validated ranking, evaluation, and governance

workflow.objective: collect bias-corrected feedback and iterate ranking
acceptance_tests: confirm bias correction on a control set
workflow.do_first_because: feedback iteration runs last and must not contaminate frozen evaluation

priority_rationale.notes: frames every downstream model, label, and metric
scope is costly to change after indexing
semantic foundation for ANN, hybrid, rerank
vector search requires built ANN index
query analysis must match index analysis
high-value but depends on retrieval quality
reusable collection bias is hard to undo
leakage/overfit damage is hard to reverse
runs last to avoid eval contamination

dominance_rules.trigger: high risk_if_wrong conflicts with delivery speed
dominance_rules.rule: risk control dominates speed when risk_if_wrong>=0.80
dominance_rules.required_action: add acceptance tests and human review before proceeding
dominance_rules.example: ship RAG faster vs add a grounding/faithfulness gate -> add the gate

dominance_rules.trigger: value-first ordering would precede an unmet prerequisite
dominance_rules.rule: true dependency order dominates value-based ordering
dominance_rules.example: build RAG before reranking validated -> sequence rerank first

dominance_rules.trigger: numeric precision tempts an unsupported label
dominance_rules.required_action: downgrade to heuristic unless an eligible source supports the label
dominance_rules.example: label scores observed without OBSERVED_DATA -> keep heuristic

dominance_rules.trigger: a step is ready to lock but QA is incomplete
dominance_rules.required_action: run acceptance tests and validation before any lock
dominance_rules.example: hard-lock metrics before significance testing -> block until tested

dominance_rules.trigger: risk, irreversibility, or low confidence crosses review thresholds
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation above review thresholds
dominance_rules.required_action: escalate to a reviewer and record the decision
dominance_rules.example: auto-accept a reused pool flagged for bias -> require human review

dominance_rules.trigger: adding more nodes/edges strains schema consistency
dominance_rules.rule: schema stability dominates raw population volume
dominance_rules.required_action: stop adding objects and repair schema consistency first
dominance_rules.example: add edges that break dependency acyclicity -> fix structure first

dominance_rules.trigger: output formatting tempts prose or markdown
dominance_rules.required_action: emit strict JSON only, no markdown or commentary
dominance_rules.example: add explanatory text outside JSON -> remove it

dominance_rules.trigger: a claim lacks an eligible source
dominance_rules.required_action: attach a resolvable source ref or exclude the claim
dominance_rules.example: assert experimentally_validated without benchmark evidence -> exclude

dominance_rules.required_action: follow the workflow order even if a local shortcut looks faster
dominance_rules.example: tune reranker before first-stage recall fixed -> sequence recall first

dominance_rules.trigger: a score appears without explicit inputs
dominance_rules.rule: explicit formula inputs dominate hidden assumptions
dominance_rules.required_action: store every variable used and recompute from formulas
dominance_rules.example: set final_importance by hand -> recompute from node_score_formula

anti_rework_rules.rule: resolve the information need before locking corpus scope
anti_rework_rules.rationale: scoping to the wrong need forces re-scoping and re-indexing
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: corpus locked while need still ambiguous
anti_rework_rules.example: scope a web crawl before deciding the task is known-item search

anti_rework_rules.rule: derive competency questions before populating nodes
anti_rework_rules.rationale: missing questions cause node rework and gaps
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: nodes added with no CQ coverage
anti_rework_rules.example: build nodes then discover the KB cannot answer an evaluation question

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix corpus scope before choosing representation
anti_rework_rules.rationale: analyzer chosen for the wrong language mix forces reindex
anti_rework_rules.example: pick a stemmer before the corpus language set is known
rebuild HNSW because the encoder was swapped after indexing

anti_rework_rules.rule: store all formula variables before computing scores
anti_rework_rules.rationale: missing variables make scores inconsistent and force recompute
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: computed score present without its inputs
anti_rework_rules.example: set risk_score with no risk_if_wrong stored

anti_rework_rules.rule: validate first-stage recall before tuning reranking
anti_rework_rules.rationale: reranking cannot recover docs missing from candidates
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: reranker tuned on a low-recall candidate set
anti_rework_rules.example: optimize a cross-encoder while first-stage recall@100 is far below target

anti_rework_rules.rule: create relevance judgments before computing metrics
anti_rework_rules.rationale: metrics without labels are undefined and get recomputed
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: metric scores reported with no qrels
anti_rework_rules.example: report nDCG before any relevance judgments exist

anti_rework_rules.rule: run acceptance and significance tests before any lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: locking unvalidated results forces costly downgrade later
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: soft/hard lock set before tests pass
anti_rework_rules.example: lock a model choice before significance testing the gain

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete validity and fairness governance before serving
anti_rework_rules.rationale: serving an overfit or biased ranking causes production rollback
anti_rework_rules.example: deploy a model tuned on the test set, then roll back after audit

anti_rework_rules.rule: collect feedback only after evaluation is frozen and bias-corrected
anti_rework_rules.rationale: uncorrected feedback contaminates evaluation and training
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: raw clicks fed into metrics or training
anti_rework_rules.example: use position-biased clicks as ground truth, corrupting nDCG

acceptance_tests: impact set computed

no new failures introduced
posterior consistent with formula
downgrade recorded and revalidation scheduled
reviewer decision recorded

human_review_required_for: test collection reuse beyond valid system population

test_cases.input_summary: single information need over a small scoped corpus
reused test collection at risk of overfit

lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade hard_lock only after human review, validation rerun, and change-control record
